summary: End-to-end testing of Cycling Segment Tracker 2 backend (17 pytest cases) and frontend (Dashboard, Segments, Rides, Leaderboards, Backup). Backend: 17/17 pass after fixing one CRITICAL bug — ObjectId leaking into POST /api/rides response (Pydantic serialization 500). Frontend: all pages render, navigation works, GPX upload flows for both segments and rides work, effort detection within 30m radius confirmed end-to-end, backup export downloads JSON, restore replaces data. Two frontend issues found: (1) Leaderboards defaults to current year (2026) so existing efforts in older years aren't shown until user manually selects year, and (2) nested <button> inside <button> in Segments list causes a React hydration warning.

minor.issue: FIXED in this iteration — was returning 500 (PydanticSerializationError: bson.ObjectId) whenever effort detection produced any effort, because insert_one mutates the dict adding _id. Patched server.py line ~488 to pop _id before appending to all_efforts.

ui_bugs.issue: Default year is new Date().getFullYear() (2026). When efforts exist only in past years, page shows 'No efforts for this year' and best-effort-card is hidden until user manually changes year. Also the controlled <select value={year}> can hold a value (2026) that isn't in its <option> list, causing a value/options mismatch.

Hydration/DOM warning: <button data-testid='segment-delete-*'> is nested inside the parent <button data-testid='segment-item-*'>. Browser/React warns 'In HTML, <button> cannot be a descendant of <button>'. Refactor outer row to a clickable <div>/<a> or render the delete control outside the row button.

Recharts logs 'width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' when ResponsiveContainer mounts before its parent has a size (e.g., before a segment is selected). Cosmetic console warning only.

action_items: Leaderboards.jsx: when efforts load, set year to the most recent year present in efforts (e.g., years[0] if state year not in years).
Segments.jsx: avoid nesting a <button> inside another <button> — convert the row container to a non-button (div/a with role='button') or move the delete action outside the row.

Optional: in /api/segments upload path, the same MongoDB _id mutation pattern exists when inserting newly-detected efforts for existing rides. It does not surface today (response only returns the segment), but is a latent bug — apply the same _id pop defensively.
Optional: Recharts ResponsiveContainer should have a guaranteed minHeight or render only when points exist.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: db.efforts.insert_one mutates eff_doc adding bson.ObjectId; any code path that returns that dict via FastAPI/Pydantic will 500. One occurrence patched in upload_ride; consider using a small helper that strips _id, or insert a copy.

Detection algorithm in detect_efforts uses a simple linear scan and bails as soon as ride wanders away from segment_end. For long rides with multiple passes this should be fine but won't capture overlapping/reverse passes — acceptable for the stated MVP scope.
POST /api/restore performs delete_many + insert_many without a transaction; if insert fails mid-way the DB is left empty. Acceptable for single-user local app but worth documenting.
No pagination / limits on list endpoints (to_list(10000)). Fine at current scale.
Frontend ride upload component should expose data-testid='rides-list' (verified present) and 'rides-search' (verified present) — both work.
updated_files: /app/backend/server.py (one-line fix to strip _id after insert_one in /api/rides effort loop)
seed_data_creation: Tests use synthetic in-memory GPX (TEST_SEG, TEST_RIDE_WITH_EFFORT, TEST_RIDE_NO_EFFORT). Module-scoped fixture wipes DB via /api/restore at module start and end. After UI testing, DB was wiped via /api/restore with empty payload.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covers segments/rides/efforts/backup/stats. Run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v. The fixture wipes the DB via /api/restore — do NOT run against production data. The only known frontend gap is Leaderboards default-year and nested-button hydration warning; both are non-blocking but should be fixed.
rca of the issue: POST /api/rides returned 500 whenever a ride contained at least one detected effort. Root cause: motor's AsyncIOMotorCollection.insert_one mutates the input document by adding `_id: ObjectId(...)`. The handler then appended that mutated dict to all_efforts and returned it via a Pydantic response_model=RideDetail; pydantic_core could not serialize bson.ObjectId, raising PydanticSerializationError -> 500. Reproduction: upload a segment whose start/end points lie on a ride's track; upload a ride GPX with timestamps traversing those points within 30 m. Mitigation applied: after each `await db.efforts.insert_one(eff_doc)` in /api/rides, call `eff_doc.pop('_id', None)` before appending to all_efforts. Verified by re-running the full pytest suite (17/17 pass) and end-to-end UI flow.
